utterances.text: Your Honours, if we could please tender the blank map as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The map is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P647, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you to just identify some locations on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And it might assist if we zoomed in a little bit, please, Madam Registrar, on the more populated part of the map. And perhaps scrolled a little bit to the left. Sorry, other way. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sir, the first location I want to you indicate for us is the area described in some reports as Sarajevo Centar or centre?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: Sarajevo Centar refers to the municipality of Sarajevo. It's the central part of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Again with Mr. Usher's assistance, I'm going to ask you to mark that part of the map, please.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: Roughly speaking, this would be the surface covered by the Centar municipality of Sarajevo. It's this part, the central part of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. If you could draw or write, please, an SC next to that circle?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: The next location I want you to identify for us, please, is Bolnicka Street?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: That's the street that leads to the Sarajevo hospital. It's in the Kosevo area, and it would be approximately in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Could you just draw a B next to that line, please?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Some of the reports refer to just the town centre, where would that be, and is it -- well, is it any different from Sarajevo Centar?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: What I have just delimited is the area covered by the Centar municipality in Sarajevo. If you are talking about the centre of the town, that includes the buildings and the features that are actually in the central part of town. The central part of town, strictly speaking, this would be this area here.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Just below the circle you've drawn, could you please put the letters TC?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you. The next location I'm interested in is Nikola Tesla Street?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: I can't remember where that street is located. I think it's in the territory of the Novi Grad area or Novi Sarajevo, but I don't know where it is exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Could you mark for us, please, the area of Novi Grad.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you mark for us the area of Novo Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you also mark for us the Bulevar Mese Selimovica Street?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: Bulevar Mese Selimovica is the central street that leads from Sarajevo in the direction of Ilidza. This would be the street here.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can you mark that please with BMS.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you mark, please, for us, the area of Stari Grad?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: With an SG. Thank you. Can you just indicate for us now, please, the areas of -- or the streets Kosevo and Tin Ujevic streets?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: This is the part called Kosevo, and there's a street called Kosevo that runs to the central part of town from here. There's a street, Tin Ujevic Street, that runs to the Kosevo Hospital, that's about here.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. The circle that you've just drawn, could you draw a line away from that circle up to a -- a blank part of the map up near the top, and could you please mark that with TU?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you. The next area, please, is Sokolovici?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: Sokolovici is here. The map should be shifted a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: We'll pause there for a moment. I won't move the map just yet, sir. We'll come back to Sokolovici. And finally, for this map, Jajacka Street?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: I don't know where that street is exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. Finally, sir, just in relation to this map and the areas that you've marked on it, which force or forces held these parts of the city?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: The central part of town inside all of these circles. It would look like this more or less. So this part of town was, roughly speaking, under the ABiH. These marginal areas were covered by the units of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can you draw a line from that inner circle that you've drawn up to the top of the map and put ABiH, please?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, you will recognise the locations I have described as municipalities relating to impact sites contained in the various reports that you reviewed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Were the impact sites and the reports that you reviewed in the -- in that part of Sarajevo controlled by the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: On site investigations could only be carried out in territory under the control of the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours, could this marked map please be tendered as a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This marked map is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit P648, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, Madam Registrar. And when that's done, could we please have P647 back up on the screen again. And if we could zoom out so that we have -- I am sorry. I'm sorry, Your Honours, if we could please have P439 on the screen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise that map as an area of Sarajevo and its surrounds?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: Well, you can recognise the silhouette of the surface covered by the town of Sarajevo, and you can also recognise the surrounding places.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to note some more locations. If you find that we need to go zoom in closer to the map to do that, please let us know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: In fact, I wonder if we could begin just by zooming in maybe to about 80 per cent of the coverage of the map, please, Madam Registrar. That's fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: The first location I want you to mark, sir, is -- and please excuse my pronunciation, is Grdonj?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: Grdonj. Grdonj is a hill above Sarajevo approximately here. However, it seems to me that the previous map depicted the names of the hills and other features much better than this one, it seems to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, Your Honours, could we please go to P647. And if we could enlarge, please, the top right-hand third of the map. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sir, do you see the area of Grdonj on there? If you could mark that for us, please.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Which forces held that hill?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: Facing the town it was the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Facing the northern side of the hill, it was the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you. If you could just mark a G inside that circle, please.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: The next location, please, is Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And you could mark an M within a circle, please.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And which forces held that area?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: That area was held by the forces of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you. The next location, please, is Mount Trebevic.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And if you could mark that with a T.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And which forces held that area?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: Again, the slopes towards the town were held by the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. However, almost the entire area of Trebevic mountain was held bit forces of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, the next location please is Vojkovici?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: We have to scroll up a little.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Before we do that, sir, because we will lose your markings if we do that, let me go through some other locations in case they can be marked on this map. Gavric Brdo.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, Gavric Brdo is here. Approximately here in the direction of the airport.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And which forces held that area?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: Gavrica Brdo was held by the forces of the Army Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Biosko?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: Biosko, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you. And which forces held that area?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: Again the forces of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Doglodi?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: This is Doglodi.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you. And which forces held that area?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: The Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: The next location is Vraca.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Marked with a V, thank you. And which forces held that area?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: That area facing the town, that's where the line was and closer to the town was the area held by the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And the hill slopes again were held by the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, if you could mark that with an I.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Which forces held that area?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: The Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: The next location, please, is Vidikovac.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Perhaps with a VK.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: This is Vidikovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you. And which forces held that area?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: That area was actually one of the peaks of Mountain Trebevic directly overlooking the town and that's the area that was also held by the Army Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And finally on this map, please, Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If you could mark that with an L. Thank you. And which forces held that area?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: The Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: That you have. Your Honours, if that map could please be admit as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P649, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Madam Registrar. And could we please have one more time P647 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: There was one location which we weren't able to -- or you weren't able to identify, sir, on the zoomed in version of the map that we've just had on the screen, that was Nedzarici can you see it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Mr. Usher -- thank you, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas, it looks like the usher is trying to get your attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Usher. We need to zoom in? Maybe on the top left-hand third of the screen. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are welcome.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, I think that we should scroll up a little. No, no, scroll down rather. Go on. Go on. Well, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And which forces held that area?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: That area was held by the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Usher. Your Honours, if that could please be tendered as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P650, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, Madam Registrar. Your Honours, that concludes the matters I wish to raise with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. If I could ask Madam Registrar a quick question, if I bring up an exhibit that has been previously marked on and wish to put new markings on that exhibit and give it a new Exhibit number, will that offend the original exhibit? Great.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'd like to start off by asking a -- one very brief question with regard to your statement in the interview process that you went through with Mr. Thomas in giving that statement. When you gave the statement to Mr. Thomas, did you engage in a series of questions and answers at that time? Did he ask you a specific question to which you gave him a specific answer which was written down?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: I had been given a number of documents which I reviewed, and then I provided explanations about the documents, what they contain, how they were produced, and what were the usual and customary procedures to be used in the drafting of such documents. I also knew some people who had been involved in the drafting of those documents and I put that in my statement. And there were no other questions with this regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The reason I ask you is because Mr. Thomas asked you if you were asked the same questions today, would you give the same answers, and in going through your statement, I don't see there to be any questions -- or, rather, it is -- I suppose it's answers. So I just wanted to make sure that I understood the process that you'd gone through when you had the interview with Mr. Thomas, which I now understand better. And it would be fair to say -- it would be fair to say that reviewing your statement, as you look at your statement, you view your statement to be correct with regard to the informations contained therein?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: I had been given a series of documents. I asked what my task was, and then I was told that I would be asked to provide explanations about each of the documents. In any case, what you can read in my statement is what I wrote at the time when the statement was issued and that is that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the statement that you made during the interview process, I note that you speak, it says here, Languages used during -- in the interview, both English and Bosnian. Am I to understand that you are fluent in both of those languages, sir?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether this could be described as fluent but, yes, I can express myself in English. I can understand English. If I am not familiar with a particular word, I ask for explanation. Providing the explanation is given, then I can understand everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excellent. That could be of some help to me in future depending on the way that we go. In your statement, you draw a distinction, as I understand it, between the forensic, what I'm going to call department, and the KDZ department; correct.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And your function was in the forensic aspects of the investigation true?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I guess we can get an explanation of what KDZ is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the forensic --

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: KDZ is the anti-bomb squad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. With regard to the forensic department, your duties, your department's duties were to collect evidence from a scene of an incident, true? You were not engaged in analysis at that time? Let me back up, because I've actually asked you two questions in one and I don't mean to do that. It was your function to collect evidence from the scene; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: I was the chief of that department. In my department I had experts for various jobs, and there are also people who were looking for traces of explosives and explosive devices. What I'm saying is that there were people in my department who were experts and could be called experts for certain things. I was the one who would assign those men to particular crime scenes, and I, myself, was not the one who would go to the crime scene to collect evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Understood. Understood. Now, apart from your team, there was also the KDZ team; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: When we were dealing with explosions, we always sent a KDZ team. My people would rarely go to such crime scenes. It would mostly be the KDZ men who would be sent to such places.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I think you've explained to the Chamber, but since we are now dealing with the KDZ men, what was the KDZ team's function? What were they to do? Are they particular with regard to dealing with explosions?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: In the first part of my written statement you will find a description of the function of the Ministry of Interior and its organisational units. And there, I explain that within the police administration there was an independent department for KDZ, and there was another independent department for forensics. I was the chief of that department for forensics, and our task - according to rules of service of the public security - we had to investigate grave crimes which involved the killing of more than one person, and we also were involved in the investigation of crime scenes where major material damage was inflicted or where the perpetrator was an unknown person. That was the forensics department. Whereas the KDZ department functioned in the following way: They had to find and deactivate or remove any explosive devices or mines. In the course of the war when there were a large number of explosions happening in Sarajevo, the KDZ took over the role that they could -- they were only ones to perform and that was to investigate such explosions. Based on the information on the collected particles of the explosives, they were charged with identifying the types of explosives. And based on the traces on the crime scene, they were tasked with determining the direction from which the explosive had been fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. You state in your statement at paragraph 14 the following, "At the local level (CSB)," what does that stand for?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: This is the security services centre, a service that was at a lower level than the Ministry of the Interior, and it covered the city of Sarajevo. Within that area there were some 15 municipalities, each with its own police service. The republican Ministry of Interior was in charge of the entire territory of the former republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and was involved in investigating only the gravest of crimes; whereas, the security services centre was involved in investigating only minor crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think it would behoove you as well as the questioning process if you would pay attention to the question asked, answer that question, if you need to expanded that answer, that's fine with me, but I'd asked you a specific question about the CSB. There are a number of other things you say here, so just so we can get an understanding of what each one of these acronyms mean it can be of some help. The next you say is. "... and SJB." What does SJB stand for?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: Public security station. Or a police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. There were also forensic and KDZ technicians, and I believe that you described to us and explained to us what the letters KDZ mean. Now, you say the following: "... who were trained to carry out some easy forensic investigations." And I'd like to focus on that to understand what you mean by easy forensic investigations.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: CSB or Security Services Centre was responsible for a territory that consisted of 15 municipalities. Under the law, they were tasked with investigating any security incidents that take place in their territory. If such an incident involved more than one dead, if there was a killing perpetrated by an unknown perpetrator, or if the incident involved a major damage or if the incident involved a foreigner, then they would inform the Ministry of Interior, which would be my forensics, and then my people would be sent to the crime scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me --

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: If the situation was different --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I appreciate your answer, but your answer is really non-responsive to the question that I've asked. The question that I asked you was what you mean by "easy forensic investigations," since you say in your statement they were trained to carry out some easy forensic investigations. That's all I'm asking you at the moment. What do you mean by that statement? What is the distinction between easy forensic investigations and hard forensic investigations. I guess. I'm guessing because I obviously don't know, that's why I'm asking the question.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: For example, if we are talking about a burglary, or if two persons were involved in a physical fight, if the perpetrators were known and the consequences of the events minor, then we would call this minor or easy incidents. In any case, the perpetrators have to be known for an incident to be qualified as "easy," as it were, incidents, and as a rule they were under the jurisdiction of the CSB.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. With regard to KDZ technicians, KDZ technicians as you've explained it to us were technicians who were involved in what I would call explosive incidents; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That is not a simple burglary, now, is it, that is something a bit more complex; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So with regard to the KDZ technicians that are contained in your explanation at paragraph 14, I take it that what you had, and correct me if I'm wrong, what you had was you had a merging of your forensic technicians to work with the KDZ technicians with regard to what I will term "explosive incidents"? The two departments worked together for those purposes?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: In the ministry, there were two independent departments. The first one was the forensic department and the other one the KDZ department. However, in a CSB there was a single department which merged the two, both the forensic department and department for KDZ. That was just one department.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Guy-Smith. We'll take a break and come back at quarter to 6.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Vejzagic, I'd like to give you a gentle thought. Court concludes today at 7.00, and I would like to do my best to be able to finish my examination of you today so that you are not inconvenienced. So if you will listen to my questions and answer the question that I've, asked I'd appreciate. I think it might go a bit quicker, also, of course, if you need to explain any of your answers, please feel free to do so. Okay? You've indicated to us that you are not an expert when it comes to issues concerning artillery shells; is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Can you tell us by any chance, how many charges there are in a 120-millimetre mine before its fired, if you know?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: I really wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when I said "mine" I was referring to the mortar shell.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: A mine, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I want to make sure that we are using the same language. Have you personally learned the science of azimuth in terms of the arc and range of mortar shells?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: I served in the JNA. I went to the school of reserve officers, and part of our training dealt with that. I don't remember that I had some specific training in ranges and arcs and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So we are clear, you'd indicated that with regard to the range of an artillery shell, you've indicated, I believe it's page 38, lines 23 to 25, that the smaller the angle the farther the range; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: Well, I know that from physics.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: That the range is very much influenced by the quantity of the charge, and the angle of the barrel.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to the answer that you gave to Mr. Thomas concerning the angle, I take it that as far as you understand, that's an accurate statement, which is the smaller the angle, the farther the range in terms of its trajectory?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: The smaller the angle, no, the range is not shorter. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. I take it it would be the larger the angle, the farther the range?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: The smaller the range, no, no, no. If your angle is anything from 0 to 90 degrees, then the biggest range should be at the angle of 45 degrees, and if the angle is even wider, then the range is smaller. But that will also depend on the force of the charge, how many -- how much gases will develop when the shell is fired, and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to the information that you have about the reports that you looked at which show what I'd say are fragments of a mortar shell, you can't tell us as you sit here today what the force of any of those charges was, can you?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: I am not an expert in the area. Really, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. In your statement at paragraph 55, you discuss markings on shells, and you state: "Approval for production was issued by the Federal Secretariat for National Defence." Now, my question to you is, is do you know when you are discussing the Federal Secretariat for National Defence, would that have been the Ministry of Defence, or would have that have been some other organ of the government?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: I claim this based on what I remember from 1972 when I served in the JNA. At that time, we were told about the procedures applied to the designing and obtaining technical data, and then the -- we were also told that the Federal Secretariat for National Defence would eventually grant approval for production.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the Federal Secretariat for National Defence was an organ of the government in the former Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Once that particular state ceased to exist, do you know who was responsible for approval of production of these particular items?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. With regard to the Krusik factory, which is the factory that you have indicated in paragraph 56 of your statement, you indicate that you believe that they still produce military equipment for Serbia. And you refer the reader to a website in your statement. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. First of all, are you aware of the fact that the website that you referred us -- that you refer the reader to is a website for a private company that presently produces springs, and by that I mean metal springs?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: No, when I remember that it was Krusik Valjevo, I searched the internet, and it seems to me that when I found the web page I saw that mines and explosives were still on their product range.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, during the period of the war, do you know whether or not the factory, the Krusik factory, was a government factory or a private factory?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, we can't take that any further.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, could we please have P649 up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, what I'd like to do, first of all, if we could, is with the help of the usher and using a different colour, you mentioned on a number of occasions where the ABiH was in terms of what side of the slope they were on. I think the first place you mentioned that was in the area that you've designated as G, in which you indicated that the ABiH was on one side of the slope and that the VRS was on the other side; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And could you -- I hope we are using a different colour, I hope we are using red now. Could you mark in red on which side of the circle in which there's a letter G the ABiH was stationed?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And could you put an ABiH underneath that, please.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. I believe that you indicated there were -- there was another place where, once again, the ABiH was stationed. Do you see any other places on the map as it presently exists where there were ABiH military?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: The BiH Army forces were deployed along the whole length of the narrow stretch of the town of Sarajevo. Sarajevo is in a valley, and the forces of the Army Republika Srpska were on the hill slopes around Sarajevo, and the forces of the army Bosnia-Herzegovina were within the city. For example, they were on -- at the foot of Vidikovac, those were actually the slopes, and this is facing the town, and this is the top of this mountain called Trebevic. From Vidikovac a view extends of the whole city of Sarajevo. You have it like in the palm of your hand. And at the foot of that, Vidikovac, there was the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and also on Vraca which is a hilltop very close to Sarajevo. That's also where the BiH Army forces were stationed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Moving towards your left on this particular document, could you indicate to the Chamber where else the you would find the forces of the ABiH stationed?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: I must say that I was never on a single frontline during the war. I never inspected the forces of any of the army. However, in view of the stories and while I resided in Sarajevo, I could see where fire was coming from because you could see fire. When bullets were fired, you could see the tracing bullets as if it was a guided missile. You could see that, you could see smoke after a missile was fired, and based on that information I'm providing my information. I know that you could not pass through a certain areas of town because you would be targeted by the fire mines of the Army Republika Srpska. So in rough outlines, I would say that this was the central part of the town, and maybe we could also say that fighting was taking place on a hilltop called Zuc. Zuc was eventually taken. So this was the area, roughly speaking. And the rest was all under the control of the Army of Republika Srpska. This is a very rough sketch because I'm not really very familiar with the lines. I suppose that your military experts would provide you with better information. I'm providing my information as a common citizen who lived in the town who was targeted, who was observing the smoke to see where the fire came from, who was listening to the stories about the sniper fires for which you could not pass through certain parts of the city and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could you please slow down, Mr. Vejzagic. If I may just ask, if you don't mind --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Absolutely not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You seem to be saying, sir, that you are determining the lines occupied by the ABiH by the smoke of the fire that you used to see. My question to you is how did you know that particular smoke from fire came from an ABiH and not from a VRS gun or whatever machinery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, a citizen who lived in Sarajevo at the time could quite clearly see from the surrounding hills or could see shooting from the surrounding his. If there were tracer bullets, then you have a light signal, you can see where the bullets is coming from. When you fire, you can also hear the sound. You can see a flame. You can see smoke, and you can see where a shell impacts. So it's very clear, you can see which locations are being used to fire on Sarajevo from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand that. I understand that. My question is slightly different from that. My question is, when you see that fire, when you see that smoke, how do you determine that that smoke comes from a VRS army shell and not from an ABiH army shell? You just see fire. And the reason I'm asking you this question is because in your answer to Mr. Guy-Smith's question, you said you determined the lines occupied by the ABiH by the fire that came out. Now, when fire comes -- if that is the only criterion you are using, my question then is: How do you know that this smoke that I see is from a VRS machine-gun and not an ABiH machine-gun?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the smoke is identical regardless of the weapon that it comes from. This would just be a conclusion on the basis of logics. The flame that you can see faces Sarajevo. The ABiH directed its weapons at the hills, so we couldn't see those weapons and the flashes from those weapons. If there was -- if there were trace of bullets that were used, then you could see that these bullets were coming from Vidikovac from the hill and not from the positions of the ABiH which were hundred metres -- or several hundred metres below that position.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Looking at the map, can you see the area that says Kobilja Glava, which is?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Is that a -- first of all, is that an area that has some elevation above the town of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's the area above Sarajevo. It's a hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And was that hill controlled by the ABiH during the war period?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: To be quite frank, I don't know. But I think that the lines were somewhere around here in the vicinity of Kobilja Glava, but I never passed through that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Can we have this marked as Defence next in order. I'm sorry, could we have this moved into evidence as Defendant's next in order, not marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we mark -- this map is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D61, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to understand something if I could, and perhaps you could be of some assistance to us. You have identified your investigations as areas where there were crime scenes; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: The documents I reviewed, well, I've confirmed that these were documents that would be drafted if you went to carry out an onsite investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: My question to you is, considering the fact that you have shown us now on two separate maps where the ABiH army was, did you have an agreement with the army with regard to what would be considered to be a zone of warfare as opposed to what would be considered to be a crime scene where your jurisdiction began and their jurisdiction ended, or vice-versa?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether there was such an agreement. But I know that the rule was as follows: If there were any incidents in the area of the frontlines, then the military police would be responsible for that. The regular police was never present at those first -- at those frontlines. This was something for the military police to deal with. As to whether there were any agreement, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say "frontlines," was that an area that was defined in terms of distance as to what a frontline would be? How was that defined, the frontline? And by that I'm referring really to the depth in terms of metres or kilometres that defined the frontline.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The incidents, the reports that you reviewed, in large measure cover a period in the summer -- I should put it this way, the late spring and early -- in summer of 1995; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: That's probably correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During that period of time, during the late spring and early summer months of 1995, that was a time when there was relatively active fighting between the VRS and the ABiH; correct? It was one of the more intense periods?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: I don't know how I would assess it. We were under fire every day, so I don't know whether it was more or less intense at the time. There was ongoing fighting at all times.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There was a point in time when the ABiH actually gained territory in 1995, true?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I remember that the lines in 1992 and 1995 didn't change until the very end of the war. In 1992 in the town, well, the places that were dangerous to pass through in 1992 and 1993 were also dangerous to pass through in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. With regard to those times that there were victories obtained by the ABiH, did you hear of those through the news media?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, there were victories outside of Sarajevo, some territory was taken outside of Sarajevo, the frontlines were moved in those areas, but as for Sarajevo itself, I don't remember the lines being moved at all. I don't remember any such victories. On the whole, this is information I obtained from the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. With regard to the investigation of any explosive site, using the same term, I think I said explosive incident, I apologise, explosive incident site, the teams that would arrive to investigate were both civilian teams, that you've mentioned before, and by that I'm talking about your forensic team as well as the KDZ; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: I've already provided you a detailed explanation of the procedure followed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Sure. To your knowledge, were on occasion international teams also present at the explosive incident sites?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: I know that an international team was involved when there was an explosion in which over 60 people were killed on one occasion. The next event or incident concerned 68 individuals more or less who were killed in Markale 2. I know about this for sure because I participated, and another team cooperated with this international team, but from colleagues who were on the site I heard that sometimes international monitors also became involved in onsite investigations, onsite investigations that concerned incidents in which fewer people were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the Markale incident that you referred to, did you hear in the media that there was some, initially, confusion with regard to who was considered to be responsible for the Markale incident?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: I heard about that, I saw the news on television. I was shocked by the fact that such news was relayed. They said that Bosnian soldiers had brought in dead, that they had used puppets or dolls, that the explosion had been staged and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm sure you were shocked by that. Did you ever hear any criticism of the conclusions that were raised concerning Markale 2 in terms of who was responsible for Markale 2 in the media? And specifically by any international individual or entity that had engaged in an investigation of Markale 2?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: In that case, it was said that ABiH forces had deliberately shelled Markale as a result of which a number of people were killed, but with the assistance of international monitors who were active at the time, and they actively observed the artillery positions of both sides. With their assistance, it was established that there was no shelling by the ABiH at the time. It was established that there was shelling by the VRS, and with their assistance it was established that the shelling was from their side and that was relayed by the media, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see. So with regard to information that was relayed by the media, there were in fact conflicting reports concerning who was responsible for this shelling that were relayed by the media?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: The Republika Srpska media stated that the Muslims were firing on themselves, were shelling themselves. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, do you know whether with regard to those incidents in which international teams were invited to investigate, whether or not any teams were invited to investigate from Serbia with regard to what had happened?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: I don't remember anyone from Serbia or from the VRS participating in the onsite investigations into such incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to -- independent of Serbia, with regard to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia do you recall any invitations being made to them to come to investigate issues concerning explosive incidents?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: When onsite investigations were carried out, well, I know that no one from that side was invited to participate in the investigation. The judge who carried out the onsite investigation decided on who would participate in the incidents. Whether anything was subsequently done, whether any other subsequent procedure was followed by others, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say that the Judge made the determination who would investigate or who was invited to investigate the onsite, that judge was a judge who was a part of the ABiH entity; correct? The political entity?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean by a political entity. But at the time the judiciary was functioning and the court had territorial jurisdiction, and they carried out onsite investigations as they did in other areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the territorial jurisdiction, what I was referring to -- what I meant -- when I said "political entity," I was referring to -- to what I would call that part of what was considered to be Bosnia as a political state at that time. That was the functioning court system; correct? I mean, admittedly there was a war going on, but there was a functioning court system within the state of Bosnia; right?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: The state was called the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the court functioned within that state.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. To your knowledge during the period of the war, were any invitations made at any time to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia to come investigate those matters that were being investigated by a judge from the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: I never heard anything about such things.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I could have a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As always, thank goodness for Mr. Mair.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: One last area which is, with regard to the markings that are found on the shells, the fragments, you had mentioned in your statement that there were a series, one of the markings may have indicated a series from which they came. And I take it when you said that you meant a production series? Are you following me?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: I said that I'm not an expert on that field. I was the head of the department in which there were experts on that field. They used information obtained from the books and documents that they had. These were documents that were also from the former JNA, and then on the basis of those document, they made certain claims. I would sign the relevant documents to state that competent individuals had carried out the work. They were educated individuals, they knew what they were doing, and they were authorised to act in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I take it when you say they were competent and they were educated, those individuals would be in a position to inform us with regard to what role the Ministry of Defence had, if any, in the production of these particular items?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The Ministry of Defence of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: I don't think anyone mentioned the Ministry of Defence of Serbia then, they just mentioned the markings that were interpreted on the basis of the information obtained from documents issued by the Ministry of Defence of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see. So the situation is is that the markings established the situs of the production of the item and nothing more? I'm sorry, I don't mean to be that limiting because there was more than that, there was also a year on it. I don't want to be limiting here.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, and the production series too.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the production series, my question is, did the individuals that you were dealing with who were experienced in this regard have any further information concerning what the significance was of any particular production series, whether it be a 3 or a 9 or a 7?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what that would mean exactly in the case of shells, but if something is produced in a series, then the series has been authorised on the base of the technical documents that are created for the given series. The type of material is specified, and this determines the product, gives it a certain -- certain individual characteristics, a certain amount of material is used to create certain equipment. That's a series. When you have new material, then you have a different series of products. I don't know what the exact meaning of these series is, but that is how one acted. That is how this was done in technological terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you can't tell us, as you sit here today, if there's any relationship between a series run - and by that I mean a production of a particular series - and the entity that approved that particular series run, can you?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD VEJZAGIC
utterances.text: The information concerns information from documents that date back to 1971. They are copies of those documents that were used. So no one said which entity authorised the production of a given series.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you for your time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Guy-Smith. Any re-examination, Mr. Thomas?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Vejzagic, we've come to the conclusion of your testimony now. I thank you very much for taking the time to come and testify. You are now excused, you may stand down, and please travel well back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: That concludes the evidence for today, Your Honours. There is one minor administrative matter which I would like to raise and deal with regarding the allocation of an exhibit number relating to some previous testimony, but other than that, Your Honours, I have no other matters to raise today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. You may deal with that administrative matter, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. During the course of MP-014's testimony, there was one exhibit that was comprised of four separate photographs. There was no objection to the admission of two of those photographs, and the remaining two were MFI'd. The -- we understand that the position is that the two photographs which were admitted were given an exhibit number of P599 and that we had to effectively reload the two MFI'd photographs with a new 65 ter number to which needs to be attributed a different exhibit number. So I'm in a position, Your Honours, simply to identify that the pages 3 and 4 of P599, which were marked for identification only, have been uploaded again as 65 ter Exhibit number 08234.02. And in respect of that exhibit, I seek that they be admitted and marked for identification and given an exhibit number as one exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you still want them marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, sir. I think the reason why they had to be separately uploaded was because we effectively had to split an exhibit into the part that was entered into evidence without objection, and the part of the exhibit which was objected to. They couldn't both go --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Under one number.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Under one number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, I believe you followed that. The last two pages of Exhibit 599 had been marked for identification together with the first two pages. Now, the request is to split the two, the admitted part and the marked for identification part. Can we mark the last two pages which are marked for identification, give them an exhibit number, and still mark them for identification under 65 ter 08234.02.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, those two photographs will be Exhibit P651 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Was that all, Mr. Thomas?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I've just received confirmation that that's all. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In that event, that brings us to the conclusion of today's session and we stand adjourned to Monday, the 9th of March, at 9.00 in the morning in Courtroom I. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 9th day of March 2009, at 9.00 a.m. 22 23 24
